nodes.description: Public mapping(address => uint) tracking the ether balance credited to each hodler.
Constant uint 1844690399 that gates when party() can be executed.
Payable fallback function that credits msg.value to hodlers[msg.sender] and emits Hodl.
Withdraw function that checks block.timestamp and hodlers[msg.sender], zeroes the balance and transfers it out.
Caller-controlled address used as mapping key and transfer recipient.
Miner-influenceable timestamp compared against partyTime in party().
Unchecked arithmetic credit into the hodlers mapping (overflow risk on uint).
External call sending ether to an untrusted address; state is only zeroed before the call, enabling reentrancy into the payable fallback.
Local variable holding the stored balance read from hodlers[msg.sender] before transfer.
Balance reset performed before the external transfer, forming the state-write part of the withdrawal flow.

edges.reason: msg.sender provides the mapping key for the unchecked balance credit operation.
The unchecked addition writes the credited amount into the hodlers state variable.
msg.sender is used directly as the index into the hodlers mapping.
The payable fallback executes the credit operation whenever ether is sent.
party() requires block.timestamp > partyTime, making execution dependent on a miner-influenceable timestamp.
The partyTime constant gates the only path that allows withdrawal in party().
party() directly executes the ether transfer to the caller.
The transfer recipient is the caller-controlled msg.sender.
The external transfer can re-enter the payable fallback with additional value and re-credit the hodler balance before the withdrawal completes.
The local variable value is read from hodlers[msg.sender] in party().
The transfer amount is derived from the stored balance, so the payout depends on stale state.
The balance reset operates on the same hodlers mapping entry used by the unchecked credit.

normalization_plan.reason: value is a transient local only used as the argument to the unsafe transfer operation and can be folded into that operation node.
